records.rationale: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema (addGuests.schema.ts) is z.object({bookingId, guests: z.array(z.string().email())}) with no uniqueness check, and the handler's uniqueGuests filter only removes guests matching pre-existing booking.attendees (case-sensitively via `guest === attendee.email`) or the blacklist — it never deduplicates guests within the same request. The uniqueness refine exists only in the client dialog's local ZAddGuestsInputSchema. So a direct API call with duplicated emails creates duplicate Attendee rows via createMany. Mechanism fully verifiable in the diff.

records.issue_text: [BUG] ZAddGuestsInputSchema enforces only per-string email format with no uniqueness, and the handler's filter (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) only exact-matches existing attendees, so duplicate or case-variant emails create duplicate Attendee rows. Adding 'John@X.com' when attendee 'john@x.com' already exists — reachable through the dialog, whose uniqueness check only covers the input array — persists a second attendee row for the same person who then receives two different guest emails; a direct API caller can pass the same email twice for the same result.
records.rationale: Verifiable from the diff: ZAddGuestsInputSchema is `z.object({bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email())})` — no uniqueness refinement, and the handler's dedup filter `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` is exact-match, so 'John@X.com' would pass when 'john@x.com' exists, creating a duplicate attendee row that then receives guest emails. Case-insensitive email semantics are standard; this is a real correctness defect in newly added code.
